sources.entry: GitUp - The Git interface you've been missing all your life has finally arrived.

summary.one_liner: GitUp is a macOS Git client that lets you manipulate the repository graph directly, with unlimited undo/redo, snapshots, and an open-source framework (GitUpKit) for building your own Git GUI.
summary.what_it_does: GitUp is a Git GUI for Mac that interacts directly with the Git database on disk. Its main view is a live, interactive repo graph where you can edit, reorder, fixup, and merge commits. The README says it offers unlimited undo/redo for almost all operations, including rebases and merges, and Time Machine-like snapshots for one-click rollback to earlier repo states. It also includes a visual commit splitter, a unified reflog browser, and instant search across the whole repo including diff contents. The core and UI elements are packaged as the open-source GitUpKit framework, which the README says has been used for apps such as Retcon. GitUpKit is split into a Foundation-only base layer (Core, Extensions) and an AppKit UI layer (Interface, Utilities, Components, Views).
use_cases: visually edit and reorder git commits
undo a risky git rebase or merge
roll back a repository to an earlier state
split a commit into smaller commits
search across git history and diff contents
build a custom Git GUI on macOS
how_to_run: If no developer account: delete the "Code Signing Identity" build setting of the "Application" target
Alternatively install a release via Homebrew: brew install gitup-app (not maintained by GitUp developers)
notable: Live interactive repo graph where you manipulate commits as graph nodes
Unlimited undo/redo, including rebases and merges
Time Machine-style snapshots for one-click rollback
GitUpKit framework for building other Git UIs, with a rebase engine reimplemented on a minimal libgit2 subset
caveats: Building requires code signing setup; without a developer account the build fails until the signing setting is removed
Homebrew package is not maintained by the GitUp developers
README describes it as a Mac application (AppKit UI layer is OS X only)
